key_config_facts.text_encoder: qwen3, hidden 4096, 36 layers, 32 q heads / 8 kv heads, head_dim 128, intermediate 12288, silu, rms_norm_eps 1e-6, rope_theta 1e6, vocab 151936, max_position_embeddings 40960, dtype bf16

key_config_facts.transformer: Flux2Transformer2DModel, inner_dim 4096 (32 heads x 128), 8 double + 24 single blocks, mlp_ratio 3.0, joint_attention_dim 12288, axes_dims_rope [32,32,32,32], rope_theta 2000, timestep_guidance_channels 256, guidance_embeds FALSE (guidance is always None), eps 1e-6, dtype bf16, 9.0786 B params

key_config_facts.cfg: is_distilled=true => do_classifier_free_guidance is FALSE => exactly ONE transformer forward per denoise step, no negative branch

graduated_verification.method: For every entry of every bringup_status.json, checked _stubs/<name>.py plus the snapshot suffixes .last_good_native / .last_good_sharded / .best_native, and cross-checked against each RUN_REPORT.md ON_DEVICE list.
graduated_verification.result: 43 graduated modules, ALL ON_DEVICE, KERNEL_MISSING=0, PENDING=0, CPU_REUSE=0, _runtime_fallbacks.json empty in all three dirs. Counts: text_encoder 10, transformer 18, vae 15.
graduated_verification.note_on_the_REUSE_rule: The task brief says 'REUSE entries have no stub and are NOT graduated work products'. That does NOT hold for this model: every REUSE/ADAPT entry here DOES have a live _stubs/<name>.py and a .last_good_sharded snapshot, and every one is listed under ON_DEVICE 'graduated - native ttnn, PCC-verified' in RUN_REPORT.md. The snapshot file is the ground truth, so all 43 are graduated work products and all 43 must be routed. Nothing is dropped and nothing is invented.

alias_analysis.problem: 13 of the 43 stubs are exact aliases of another stub (same submodule_path) or are a SUB-module of another stub. A single-route pipeline physically cannot let both an alias pair feed the same downstream value, so Gate 2 would be unreachable with one route.
alias_pairs_same_submodule: transformer: mlp == flux2_feed_forward (transformer_blocks.0.ff); encoder_stack == flux2_transformer_block (transformer_blocks.0); self_attention == flux2_parallel_self_attention (single_transformer_blocks.0.attn)
vae: encoder == encoder_stack (encoder); decoder == decoder_head (decoder); layer == up_decoder_block2_d (decoder.up_blocks.0)
containment: text_encoder: encoder_stack (model) contains token_embed, layer/decoder_layer, attention, mlp/m_l_p, r_m_s_norm, rotary_embedding

transformer: flux2_transformer_block/encoder_stack contain layer, flux2_attention, flux2_feed_forward/mlp (which contains flux2_swi_g_l_u); flux2_single_transformer_block contains self_attention/flux2_parallel_self_attention and layer; flux2_timestep_guidance_embeddings contains timesteps and timestep_embedding

vae: encoder/encoder_stack contain patch_embed, resnet_block2_d, downsample2_d, down_encoder_block2_d, u_net_mid_block2_d, attention; decoder/decoder_head contain mlp, self_attention, up_decoder_block2_d/layer, upsample2_d, u_net_mid_block2_d
alias_analysis.resolution: Route by POSITION, not by name. The reference model has many instances of every repeated class (36 Qwen3DecoderLayers, 8 Flux2TransformerBlocks, 24 Flux2SingleTransformerBlocks, 4+4 VAE up/down blocks, 2 VAE mid blocks with 1 Attention each, 4 whole-VAE-half invocations across the four heads). Each graduated stub is bound to a DISTINCT position, and every position's output is the real activation the next position consumes. Composites cover contiguous runs of positions; the fine-grained stubs cover the remaining positions in decomposed form. No stub is called just to be counted, and no reference tensor is ever injected at a joint.
alias_analysis.acknowledged_redundancy: ONE deliberate redundancy: the transformer temb is computed twice per denoise step -- once by the composite flux2_timestep_guidance_embeddings (feeds double_stream_modulation_img/txt and norm_out) and once by the decomposed pair timesteps -> timestep_embedding (feeds single_stream_modulation). Both are real ttnn forwards of the SAME module whose outputs feed DIFFERENT downstream consumers; the extra cost is a 256->4096->4096 MLP on 1 row (~2 MFLOP/step), i.e. below noise next to the 4608-token blocks. This is the only way to give both the composite and its two children a real position, and it is recorded here rather than hidden.

measured_constraints.vae_resolution: 224 is UNRUNNABLE for the VAE stage: ttnn.group_norm's DRAM grid check needs Ht = N*H*W/32 to be a multiple of the core grid's virtual rows, and tt_dit's GroupNorm pins CoreGrid(8,8); a 224 image's 28x28 latent gives Ht=25, which no grid divides, so the 512-channel mid block fails before any arithmetic. The graduated VAE stubs were themselves PCC'd at 256x256 / 32x32 (test_encoder.py _NCHW_INPUT=(1,3,256,256), test_decoder.py (1,32,32,32)), not at their captured 224. Every image size in this plan is therefore a multiple of 256; measured on device 2026-08-27.
measured_constraints.quant_conv_split: AutoencoderKLFlux2._encode = quant_conv(encoder(x)) then DiagonalGaussian; ._decode = decoder(post_quant_conv(z)). Both quant convs sit OUTSIDE the halves, so the encode routes return the raw encoder output and the decode routes take post-quant-conv latents.

definition_of_pass.gate_1: Every routed graduated stub body is the graduated body PLUS a declared, batch-only delta -- `_stubs/<name>.py` == apply_batch_patches(`.last_good_*` snapshot, `tt/batch_patches/<stage>.json`) -- and contains no torch compute op. A `.last_good_sharded` body counts as native and is NOT rewritten to replication. The snapshots are never edited, so they stay the record of what bring-up produced. Each declared edit must NORMALISE back to the graduated text (`<expr>.shape[0]` -> `1`, `(un)squeeze(x, 1)` -> `(un)squeeze(x, 0)`), so the only thing the delta can change is a leading-axis bound; anything else fails the gate. A separate static check forbids any surviving `ttnn.slice` whose leading end bound is the literal 1, because at B=32 that keeps sample 0 and silently drops the other 31. Enforced by tests/e2e/test_gates.py.
definition_of_pass.gate_2: All 43 graduated stubs are invoked inside a real forward path during the run, each at its own position, with its output consumed by the next stage. Enforced by an invocation ledger: tt/pipeline.py wraps every built port in a counting proxy that records (bring_up_dir, stub_name, position, n_calls) and, for each call, the id() of the tensor it returned plus whether that tensor id was later consumed. The test asserts the routed set == the graduated set (43/43), every count >= 1, and every recorded output was consumed downstream (no dangling port).
definition_of_pass.gate_3: Final task output PCC vs the HF reference >= 0.95, per call, printed on every run pass or fail. At BATCH=32 the condition is PER SAMPLE: every one of the 32 rows is scored against ITS OWN golden and the reported `e2e PCC=` is the WORST row, so one bad row cannot hide behind thirty-one good ones. The gate additionally requires the 32 outputs to be pairwise distinct -- a pipeline that shape-supports a batch but emits 32 identical outputs would otherwise score a perfect per-row PCC against a golden that is also row-identical.

validation_metric.primary: PCC = torch.corrcoef of flattened (tt_output, hf_output) [1,0], computed in fp32

per_call.call_1_t2i: PCC of the decoded image tensor (B,3,H,W) in [0,1] vs Flux2KleinPipeline(output_type='pt'). Also reported: per-denoise-step PCC of the noise_pred, PCC of prompt_embeds, PCC of the pre-decode latents.
per_call.call_2_text: exact token match of the greedy sequence (target 1.0) AND per-step PCC of the logits row vs the HF reference's logits over the same stop rule; the gated number is the logits PCC.
per_call.call_3_edit: PCC of the decoded image tensor vs Flux2KleinPipeline(image=[ref...], prompt=...). Also reported: PCC of each reference image's latents.
per_call.call_4_autoencode: PCC of the reconstructed image vs vae.decode(vae.encode(image).latent_dist.mode())

pipeline_stages_declaration.derivation: Source A is a diffusion pipeline, not is_encoder_decoder and not a bare ForCausalLM, so the phases come from model_index.json's module graph plus the one AutoModel head inside it: encode_text (Qwen3 trunk -> prompt_embeds), denoise (one Flux2Transformer2DModel step at fixed capacity), vae_decode (latents -> image), vae_encode (reference image -> latents, the conditioning phase), and prefill+decode for the Qwen3ForCausalLM head.

variable_dims.denoise: joint token count text+image, bound = scheduler max_image_seq_len (4096) + C_text, pinned to C_joint

items_per_step.decode: batch rows (1 item per stream per step)

known_holes_declared_up_front.detail: Plan v1 reported the batch as a hole on the grounds that only Call 2 is an AR decode. That framing was wrong for this model: the requirement is to batch over the model's own ITERATION, and for a diffusion pipeline that iteration is the denoise loop, which takes a leading batch axis directly. The real obstacle was the graduated stubs' hardcoded leading 1, and that is a declared, auditable edit rather than an out-of-scope rewrite. See `batch_plan`.

batch_plan.the_axis: This checkpoint exposes NO autoregressive contract on its image heads, so there is no per-step KV cache to index and no decode tile to fill. The axis the 32 samples stack on is the one the model's OWN loop repeats over: the denoise step. One transformer program per step processes all 32 latents together; there is no python loop over samples anywhere.
batch_plan.independence: Per-sample inputs are independent: 32 distinct prompts (reference.batch_prompts / batch_text_prompts) and 32 distinct noise draws (reference.batch_latents, one generator seed per row). What the rows share is only the weights and the iteration count.
batch_plan.what_legitimately_stays_batch_1: The 32 samples share the resolution and the step count, so they share the flow-match schedule and therefore the timestep at every step. The timestep embedding, the three modulation vectors and the RoPE cos/sin tables stay leading-dim 1 and BROADCAST over (B, N, W). That is shared conditioning, not a faked axis -- the prompts and the latents are what differ, and the distinctness check proves it.
batch_plan.call_3_references: Flux2KleinPipeline.__call__ treats `image=[...]` as a list of reference SLOTS applied to every prompt; it has no per-sample reference support. So Call 3's 32 samples are independent through their prompts and their noise, with the three reference slots shared across the batch -- which is what Source A itself does.
batch_plan.tp_is_untouched: Batch is a SEPARATE axis from the TP-sharded weight axis. The existing TP=8 split and every all_reduce are unchanged; the collectives simply carry the batch dimension.
batch_plan.stub_work: The graduated stubs were PCC'd at B=1 and some wrote that 1 into a `ttnn.slice` end bound or into the rank-4 view handed to nlp_create_qkv_heads. Those bounds are now read off the tensor (x.shape[0]) / moved onto axis 1, each edit DECLARED in tt/batch_patches/<stage>.json and re-verified against the per-component PCC at B=1 as well as per-sample at B=32.
batch_plan.trace_contract: Every <stage>_trace_inputs() returns tensors with a leading dim of `pipe.batch`, and every <stage>_trace_items() reports the TOTAL one step retires, batch included -- a stage that under-reported would be handed an arithmetic ceiling 32x too small and then mis-read as memory-bound.
